description.purpose: The missing piece between a closed session and the central memory (GH #101): a collector hands its day out as ONE write batch, the memory hive's writer takes ONE turn at a time, and nothing spoke both forms - so a closed day never reached memory. This hive is that translation. It decomposes the batch into single-turn episodes in the order of the day, fires each of them at the memory hive's EXISTING write lane, and keeps its own ledger so that the same batch delivered twice writes nothing the second time. It lives outside the memory hive and speaks only its documented lanes: not one line of the hive changes.
description.use_when: One per talky whose closed sessions belong in the central memory. Instantiate it and wire the ports in the SAME mutation: the talky's 'write' route into ./drain (lane in_batch), ./drain's 'episode' route into the memory hive on its in_episode lane, and ./drain's 'reject' route wherever refusals are read. It is a SECOND parent edge on the write route - whatever else consumes the batch (a summarizer, an archive) keeps consuming it. The edge that carries the batch IN owes it the provenance the memory requires: context.audience_set and context.channel. A colony wired from `channel@1` already has both in context (ADR-0002 E8) and adds nothing; anything else declares them on that edge.
description.not_in_scope: No extraction, no summarising, no judgement about what is worth remembering - append-all, exactly like the batch it consumes; what memory makes of it is the hive's business and happens later, batched. No LLM call and no provider key: the write path is synchronous and model-free by spec. No second write path into memory. No session lifecycle: the keeper closes the session, the collector produces the batch. No recall lane - this adapter only writes. And no provenance of its own: it carries the participant set and the room through, it never mints them and never defaults them to `["*"]`.
examples: PORTS - Entry: in_batch, wired as {from: <talky>, to: <drain>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'write', modifier: {set_hop: {route: 'in_batch'}, set_context: {session_id: 'hop.session_id'}}}. Exit: 'episode' -> the memory hive's in_episode lane, wired as {from: <drain>, to: <memory>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'episode', modifier: {set_hop: {route: 'in_episode'}, set_context: {session_id: 'hop.session_id', turn_id: 'hop.turn_id', happened_at: 'hop.happened_at'}}}. Exit: 'reject' -> wherever refusals are read, wired as {from: <drain>, to: <sink>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'reject'} - required, and the mutation refuses the in_batch edge without it.

a 6-turn day closes -> 6 episodes with turn_ids s1#0 .. s1#5 land in the hive's episodes table, one per turn, in the order of the day, each carrying the participant set and the room the batch arrived with
the same day is closed a second time (or the batch is replayed) -> the ledger says 6 of 6 -> NOTHING is written, the row count does not move
the session grew to 8 turns since the last drain -> only s1#6 and s1#7 are written

a day arrives over an edge that carries no context.audience_set -> nothing is parked, nothing is marked, one message leaves on 'reject' with hop.reject_reason 'missing_audience'; wire the set onto the edge and deliver the same day again and all of it lands
